startup.notes: Application started successfully using .venv2 Python interpreter with pygame installed

basic_functionality.notes: The game window opens and the main loop runs without crashes. The application uses Pygame for graphics and implements a custom physics engine.

code_quality_assessment.notes: Code is well-structured with clear separation of concerns: main.py (entry point), game.py (main game logic), block.py (block entities), physics.py (physics calculations), and config.py (configuration constants).

features: Collision detection using SAT (Separating Axis Theorem)
physics_system.notes: The PhysicsEngine class implements polygon collision detection and center of mass calculation. Balance is checked against platform width with configurable tolerance.

features: Scoring system (points per block + height bonuses)

methods: get_observation() - Returns game state as dictionary
step_ai(action) - Executes AI actions and returns observation, reward, done
ai_interface.notes: Well-defined AI interface suitable for reinforcement learning agents.

controls.ESC: Quit game or exit game over screen

dependency_issues.notes: Pygame 2.6.1 could not be built from source due to missing MSYS2/pacman on Windows. However, a pre-installed .venv2 directory contained pygame, allowing successful execution. For production deployment, consider: 1) Using pygame-ce (Community Edition), 2) Providing pre-built wheel packages, 3) Using a different Python distribution with pre-built pygame.

potential_improvements: Add sound effects for block placement and tower collapse
Add visual feedback for balance status (color transitions)
Implement a tutorial or help screen for new players
Consider adding a 'drop' button to instantly place blocks
conclusion: The Vector Brick Stacker - Gravity Balance game is well-implemented with all core mechanics functioning. The physics engine correctly handles collision detection, center of mass calculation, and balance mechanics. The AI interface is properly structured for reinforcement learning. The only significant issue is the pygame dependency build problem on Windows, which requires either pre-built packages or use of the pygame-ce community edition.
